title: Encrypted Neural Networks without Overflows
abstract: arXiv:2605.23096v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The popular Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS) scheme enables efficient private inference in neural networks by evaluating them on encrypted data. Since CKKS only supports addition, multiplication, and array rotation operations, turning neural networks into CKKS circuits requires approximating all activation functions (e.g. ReLU) with polynomials over fixed input ranges. Traditionally, these ranges are estimated via heuristic sampling techniques. In this paper, we empirically demonstrate that sampled ranges leave the CKKS network exposed to overflow events, i.e. legitimate inputs that exceed the ranges of the circuit and cause corrupted outputs, and propose an improved design technique that completely avoids them. First, we propose a practical algorithm to induce overflow events in a CKKS circuit, i.e. we automatically craft legitimate inputs that exceed the design ranges within the circuit and cause corrupted outputs. translated_title: 无溢出的加密神经网络
translated_abstract: 摘要：流行的Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS)方案通过在加密数据上评估神经网络，实现了高效的私有推理。由于CKKS仅支持加法、乘法和数组旋转操作，将神经网络转换为CKKS电路需要在固定输入范围内用多项式近似所有激活函数（如ReLU）。传统上，这些范围通过启发式采样技术估计。在本文中，我们通过实验证明，采样范围会使CKKS网络暴露于溢出事件，即合法输入超出电路范围并导致输出损坏，并提出一种改进的设计技术来完全避免这些问题。首先，我们提出了一种实用算法来诱导CKKS电路中的溢出事件，即自动构造合法输入，使其超出电路内的设计范围并导致输出损坏。作为示例，我们的方法...（摘要内容不完整）
tldr: 本文提出了一种改进的CKKS加密神经网络设计技术，通过自动诱导和避免溢出事件，确保合法输入不会导致输出损坏。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an improved design technique for CKKS-encrypted neural networks that automatically induces and avoids overflow events, ensuring legitimate inputs do not cause corrupted outputs.
